cohort: The study included 33,198 women who delivered between January and June 2020 (cases) and 188,225 women who delivered between January and June 2015-2019 (controls), excluding those with preterm delivery, birthweight <500 g, multiple fetuses, fetal malformations, chromosomal anomalies, intrauterine fetal death, maternal cancer, HIV infection, and/or inter-hospital transfers.
finding: During the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic, there were significantly increased rates of labor induction, instrumental delivery, obstetric anesthesia, NICU transfer, 5-min Apgar score below 7, shorter postpartum hospitalization, and more postpartum adverse events compared to pre-pandemic periods.
mod_finding: There was a significantly increased rate of instrumental delivery during the COVID-19 period compared with the non-COVID-19 period.
followup_time: Approximately 3-4 days postpartum (for length of hospitalization and postpartum adverse events)
